title: Impact of NAFTA Tariff Removal on Bilateral Trade Flows

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) estimated with two-way fixed effects (unit-pair and year fixed effects). The coefficient on treated × post identifies the average causal effect of NAFTA tariff removal on log bilateral trade flows.
- Why: NAFTA applies to treated country pairs after implementation. With panel data by pair and year, DID compares changes in trade for treated pairs before vs. after NAFTA to contemporaneous changes for control pairs, netting out time-invariant pair factors (e.g., distance, culture) and common time shocks (e.g., global demand).
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of NAFTA, treated and control pairs would have experienced similar trends in trade flows. We probe this with a pre-trend test and a pre-period placebo DID.
  - No anticipatory effects: No systematic change in treated pairs’ trade before implementation due to anticipation.
  - Stable composition and no spillovers: No changes in sample composition; NAFTA effects on treated pairs do not spill over to control pairs.
  - SUTVA and correct functional form: Log-linear specification appropriately captures proportional effects.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 1) Setup --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read data
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s44_data.csv"
dt <- read.csv(data_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(dt)))
dt$unit_id <- as.factor(dt$unit_id)
dt$period  <- as.integer(dt$period)
dt$treated <- as.integer(dt$treated)
dt$post    <- as.integer(dt$post)
dt$treat_x_post <- as.integer(dt$treat_x_post)
dt$y <- as.numeric(dt$y)

# Helper: cluster-robust vcov (fallback to classical if sandwich/lmtest unavailable)
get_vcov_cluster <- function(model, cluster_vec) {
  if (requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)) {
    return(sandwich::vcovCL(model, cluster = cluster_vec, type = "HC1"))
  } else {
    warning("Package 'sandwich' not available. Using classical (non-robust) variance.")
    return(stats::vcov(model))
  }
}

# Helper: extract estimate table for a named coefficient
extract_coef <- function(model, coef_name, vcov_mat) {
  beta <- coef(model)[coef_name]
  se <- sqrt(vcov_mat[coef_name, coef_name])
  tval <- beta / se
  # Normal approximation for p-value (matches coeftest default with sandwich vcov)
  pval <- 2 * pnorm(abs(tval), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ci_low <- beta - 1.96 * se
  ci_high <- beta + 1.96 * se
  list(beta = beta, se = se, t = tval, p = pval, ci_low = ci_low, ci_high = ci_high)
}

cat("Data summary:\n")
cat(sprintf("- N obs: %d | N units: %d | Years: %d to %d\n\n",
            nrow(dt), length(unique(dt$unit_id)), min(dt$period), max(dt$period)))

# 2) Main DID specifications ---------------------------------------------------
# (A) Simple DID without FE (baseline illustration)
m_simple <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post, data = dt)
V_simple <- get_vcov_cluster(m_simple, cluster_vec = dt$unit_id)
res_simple <- extract_coef(m_simple, "treat_x_post", V_simple)

# (B) Two-way fixed effects DID (unit and year FE)
# Use treat_x_post explicitly to avoid coefficient naming ambiguity
m_twfe <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = dt)
V_twfe <- get_vcov_cluster(m_twfe, cluster_vec = dt$unit_id)
res_twfe <- extract_coef(m_twfe, "treat_x_post", V_twfe)

# Print main results
cat("Main DID results (log trade as outcome):\n")
cat(sprintf("Simple DID: beta = %.4f, se = %.4f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            res_simple$beta, res_simple$se, res_simple$p, res_simple$ci_low, res_simple$ci_high))
cat(sprintf("TWFE (unit & year FE): beta = %.4f, se = %.4f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            res_twfe$beta, res_twfe$se, res_twfe$p, res_twfe$ci_low, res_twfe$ci_high))
cat(sprintf("Implied percent change (TWFE): %.2f%%\n\n", 100*(exp(res_twfe$beta)-1)))

# 3) Robustness checks ---------------------------------------------------------
# (R1) Pre-trend test: pre-period only, test group-specific linear trend
pre <- subset(dt, post == 0)
if (nrow(pre) >= 10 && length(unique(pre$period)) >= 2) {
  pre$t_center <- pre$period - mean(pre$period)
  m_pretrend <- lm(y ~ factor(unit_id) + factor(period) + I(t_center * treated), data = pre)
  V_pretrend <- get_vcov_cluster(m_pretrend, cluster_vec = pre$unit_id)
  # Coefficient name is "I(t_center * treated)"
  coef_name_pretrend <- "I(t_center * treated)"
  if (coef_name_pretrend %in% names(coef(m_pretrend))) {
    res_pretrend <- extract_coef(m_pretrend, coef_name_pretrend, V_pretrend)
    cat("Pre-trend test (pre-period only, treated-specific linear trend):\n")
    cat(sprintf("beta_trend = %.5f, se = %.5f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.5f, %.5f]\n\n",
                res_pretrend$beta, res_pretrend$se, res_pretrend$p,
                res_pretrend$ci_low, res_pretrend$ci_high))
  } else {
    cat("Pre-trend test: coefficient not identified (potential collinearity).\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Pre-trend test skipped: insufficient pre-period variation.\n\n")
}

# (R2) Placebo DID in pre-period: fake policy date at median pre year
if (nrow(pre) >= 10 && length(unique(pre$period)) >= 3) {
  uniq_pre_years <- sort(unique(pre$period))
  fake_cut <- as.integer(stats::median(uniq_pre_years))
  pre$fake_post <- as.integer(pre$period >= fake_cut)
  # Ensure variation in fake_post
  if (length(unique(pre$fake_post)) == 2) {
    pre$fake_tx_post <- pre$treated * pre$fake_post
    m_placebo <- lm(y ~ fake_tx_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = pre)
    V_placebo <- get_vcov_cluster(m_placebo, cluster_vec = pre$unit_id)
    res_placebo <- extract_coef(m_placebo, "fake_tx_post", V_placebo)
    cat("Placebo DID (pre-period only, fake policy at median pre year):\n")
    cat(sprintf("beta_placebo = %.4f, se = %.4f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
                res_placebo$beta, res_placebo$se, res_placebo$p,
                res_placebo$ci_low, res_placebo$ci_high))
  } else {
    cat("Placebo DID skipped: no variation in fake_post within pre-period.\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Placebo DID skipped: insufficient pre-period years.\n\n")
}

# (R3) Sensitivity: add group-specific linear trend in full sample
dt$t_center_full <- dt$period - mean(dt$period)
dt$treated_trend <- dt$treated * dt$t_center_full
m_twfe_trend <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + treated_trend + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = dt)
V_twfe_trend <- get_vcov_cluster(m_twfe_trend, cluster_vec = dt$unit_id)
res_twfe_trend <- extract_coef(m_twfe_trend, "treat_x_post", V_twfe_trend)
cat("TWFE + treated-specific linear trend (sensitivity):\n")
cat(sprintf("beta = %.4f, se = %.4f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], implied %%: %.2f%%\n",
            res_twfe_trend$beta, res_twfe_trend$se, res_twfe_trend$p,
            res_twfe_trend$ci_low, res_twfe_trend$ci_high,
            100*(exp(res_twfe_trend$beta)-1)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Removing tariffs lowers trade costs and should increase bilateral trade among NAFTA members.
- Magnitude: In log terms, an average treatment effect around 0.2–0.4 (roughly a 22%–49% increase = 100×(e^beta−1)) is plausible, consistent with gravity-model evidence on tariff elasticities and past estimates of NAFTA’s trade effects. The precise estimate will depend on sample composition and control pairs but should be economically and statistically significant if parallel trends hold.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Comparing trade flows before and after NAFTA for treated and control pairs.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The tariff removal under NAFTA led to a significant increase in bilateral trade flows.
